identification.summary: BRONZE EDGEWOOD is the Secureworks Counter Threat Unit (CTU) name for a suspected China-based espionage group active since at least 2018 that targets government and private enterprises across Southeast Asia [S1]. In early 2021 CTU observed it exploiting Microsoft Exchange Server at a Southeast Asian organization, deploying a China Chopper webshell and a Nishang PowerShell script to reach C2 [S1]. It is publicly linked to the Chinoxy, PCShare and FunnyDream malware families and also uses Cobalt Strike [S1]. Bitdefender's November 2020 report on the Chinoxy/PCShare/FunnyDream chain, which Recorded Future associates with its own cluster TAG-16, reports more than 200 systems affected over roughly two years [S3][S5].
identification.firstObserved: Active since at least 2018 per Secureworks CTU [S1]. Bitdefender dates the FunnyDream actor to about 2018 [S3].
identification.notes: Secureworks name; no Microsoft name is mapped in this record. Red Hariasa is the PwC name given as an alias [S1][S5]. Recorded Future's TAG-16 is a separate vendor cluster that reporting associates with the same Chinoxy/FunnyDream tooling; whether BRONZE EDGEWOOD, Red Hariasa and TAG-16 are identical is not established by the sources gathered, so facts from Bitdefender and Recorded Future are attributed to those vendors and not asserted as CTU findings [S3][S5].

attribution.sponsor: Secureworks CTU assesses the group operates on behalf of the Chinese government [S1].
attribution.confidence: Secureworks CTU: moderate confidence [S1]. Recorded Future judged TAG-16 highly likely to be a state actor, with targeting consistent with Chinese political and economic goals [S5]. Bitdefender said evidence points to a Chinese-speaking group but cautioned that attribution is difficult [S3]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: CTU states a remit covering political espionage based on its observed targeting [S1]. Recorded Future cites targeting alignment with South China Sea and Belt and Road interests and shared custom capabilities with RedFoxtrot [S5]. Bitdefender cites the tooling and infrastructure largely in Hong Kong, with some in mainland China and Vietnam [S3].

objectives: Political espionage against Southeast Asian governments and enterprises [S1]. Bitdefender describes the FunnyDream activity as long-term persistence with collection and exfiltration of sensitive documents [S3]. Recorded Future links TAG-16 targeting to regional territorial disputes and Belt and Road objectives [S5].

regions: Vietnam (most victims per Kaspersky as relayed by Security Affairs) [S3]
Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam as top three in Recorded Future data [S5]
targeting.notes: CTU gives only the general government and private enterprise focus in Southeast Asia [S1]. Country and ministry detail comes from Bitdefender, Kaspersky and Recorded Future reporting on the associated tooling and may describe a wider or different cluster [S3][S5].

capabilities.summary: Exploitation of Microsoft Exchange Server, China Chopper webshell, Nishang Invoke-PowerShellTcp.ps1 and Cobalt Strike [S1]. Custom and shared backdoors Chinoxy, PCShare (open-source RAT) and FunnyDream [S1][S3]. Bitdefender reports Chinoxy provides persistence, PCShare is used to explore hosts, and FunnyDream is the most feature-rich for data gathering and exfiltration; the Chinoxy dropper side-loads a DLL via a signed Logitech Bluetooth binary [S3].

campaigns.summary: Secureworks CTU states the group has been active since at least 2018.

campaigns.name: FunnyDream campaign reporting (Bitdefender)
campaigns.summary: Bitdefender reports a Chinese-speaking actor using Chinoxy, PCShare and FunnyDream against Southeast Asian government institutions, with over 200 systems showing the tools, and likely state-sponsored espionage. Association with BRONZE EDGEWOOD is by tooling named in the CTU description.

campaigns.name: 2021 TAG-16 activity (Recorded Future)
campaigns.summary: Insikt Group reports TAG-16, using custom malware such as FunnyDream and Chinoxy, compromised government and military organizations in Southeast Asia over roughly nine months. Cluster equivalence with BRONZE EDGEWOOD is unverified.

campaigns.name: Exchange Server intrusion in Southeast Asia (early 2021)
campaigns.summary: CTU observed BRONZE EDGEWOOD exploiting Exchange Server at a Southeast Asian organization, deploying China Chopper and Nishang, and using Cobalt Strike. The source gives only 'early 2021'; month is approximate.

diamond.adversary: Suspected PRC state-aligned espionage group assessed by Secureworks with moderate confidence [S1].
diamond.capability: Exchange exploitation, China Chopper, Nishang, Cobalt Strike, Chinoxy, PCShare, FunnyDream [S1][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Bitdefender reports infrastructure mainly in Hong Kong with some in mainland China and Vietnam for the FunnyDream activity [S3].
diamond.victim: Southeast Asian government and private enterprise [S1]; military and ministry targets in TAG-16 reporting [S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Political espionage tied by Recorded Future to South China Sea disputes and Belt and Road interests [S1][S5].
diamond.technology: Internet-exposed Microsoft Exchange servers [S1]; Windows hosts susceptible to DLL side-loading through signed binaries [S3].

gaps: Primary Secureworks CTU page for BRONZE EDGEWOOD was not found or opened; its text was seen only via Malpedia and a MISP Galaxy mirror, and the publication date is unknown [S1].
Whether BRONZE EDGEWOOD, PwC's Red Hariasa and Recorded Future's TAG-16 are the same cluster is not confirmed; Chinoxy is also linked by others to other clusters.
Bitdefender and MITRE primary pages could not be fetched (network errors); details come from search snippets and secondary coverage.
Exchange vulnerabilities (CVEs) exploited in the early 2021 intrusion were not identified; Malpedia reports no tied CVEs.
The two PwC reports listed in the imported record were not opened; their content is unverified.
No government attribution or sponsoring agency is identified; no post-2022 activity found.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is internet-facing Exchange servers and government or partner-nation networks in Southeast Asia, relevant to coalition partners and US presence in the region [S1][S5]. STEP 2: The actor persists for long periods and uses signed-binary DLL side-loading and a mix of public tools (China Chopper, Nishang, Cobalt Strike, PCShare), which complicates attribution [S1][S3]. STEP 3: Template is Exchange exploitation or phishing, then webshell or Chinoxy for persistence, then PCShare/FunnyDream for collection and exfiltration [S1][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued political and military espionage against regional governments and partners. MDCOA is use of a partner-nation foothold to reach coalition communications or planning data during a South China Sea crisis. Candidate indicators: new ASPX webshells on Exchange, PowerShell reverse shells, a signed Logitech binary loading an unexpected DLL, and registry Run key persistence [S1][S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track Exchange patching and webshell hunts across mission-partner and DIB-hosted mail systems. (2) Authorities: activity on partner-nation networks needs coordination through the owning nation and established information-sharing channels, not unilateral action. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize protecting coalition messaging and planning data sets in the region. (4) Coordination: share vendor indicators with DC3 and partner CERTs, noting cluster uncertainty between vendor names [S1][S5].

provenance.importedSummary: In early 2021 CTU researchers observed BRONZE EDGEWOOD exploiting the Microsoft Exchange Server of an organization in Southeast Asia. The threat group deployed a China Chopper webshell and ran the Nishang Invoke-PowerShellTcp.ps1 script to connect back to C2 infrastructure. The threat group is publicly linked to malware families Chinoxy, PCShare and FunnyDream. CTU researchers have discovered that BRONZE EDGEWOOD also leverages Cobalt Strike in its intrusion activity. BRONZE EDGEWOOD has been active since at least 2018 and targets government and private enterprises across Southeast Asia. CTU researchers assess with moderate confidence that BRONZE EDGEWOOD operates on behalf the Chinese government and has a remit that covers political espionage.
